science.title: Structural determinants for FAT10 activation and transfer from UBA6 to E2 enzymes
science.description: Attachment of the ubiquitin-like protein (UBL) FAT10 onto substrates targets them for proteasomal degradation. Like ubiquitin, FAT10 is activated by the E1 enzyme UBA6 then transferred to E2 enzymes, but mechanisms controlling ubiquitin versus FAT10 activation by UBA6 and FAT10 transfer onto E2s remain unclear. Using cryo-EM, we visualise all stages of FAT10 E1-E2 handover: adenylation, thiolation and transthiolation. We find that FAT10 monopolises UBA6 by out-competing ubiquitin for thiolation and blocking the adenylation domain, preventing further UBL recruitment and promoting FAT10 signalling. We profiled UBA6-compatible E2 enzymes and found FAT10 transfer is restricted to a select subset associated with specific cellular pathways. UBE2Z (USE1) showed highest activity followed by UBE2D2, UBE2J2 and UBE2S. Capturing FAT10 or ubiquitin transfer from UBA6 to UBE2Z reveals UBE2Z is highly specialised for FAT10 transfer. It simultaneously engages both FAT10 domains (UBL1 and UBL2) and co-ordinates the metabolite inositol hexakisphosphate (InsP6) bound within the UBA6 catalytic domain. This InsP6 co-ordination extends to other FAT10 compatible E2s. Together, our structural and biochemical analyses reveal regulatory mechanisms underpinning FAT10 activation and transfer. We define principles governing selective FAT10 transfer, highlighting favourable interactions with FAT10 C-terminal domain (UBL2) and stable UBA6 binding, ensuring controlled conjugation onto substrates. Cryo-EM captures FAT10 activation and transfer from UBA6 to E2 UBE2Z, revealing FAT10 monopolises UBA6. Efficient transfer requires E2 engagement of both FAT10 UBL domains, particularly UBL2, and co-ordination of InsP₆ in the UBA6 catalytic domain.

science.title: Explainable multi-model machine learning framework for tensile property prediction of FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloys
science.description: Reliable and interpretable prediction of tensile properties is critical for accelerating the design of high-entropy alloys (HEAs), yet many existing machine learning approaches emphasize predictive accuracy without sufficient consideration of physical interpretability or deployment efficiency. In this study, we propose X-HEA-ML, an explainable multi-model machine learning framework for predicting key tensile properties of FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloys, namely Young’s modulus, ultimate tensile strength (UTS), and yield strength. A dataset of 918 samples was generated using molecular dynamics simulations, incorporating compositional, microstructural, and thermomechanical descriptors. The framework integrates a diverse set of regression models, including linear models, decision trees, support vector machines, ensemble learners, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), neural networks, and kernel-based methods. All models are trained under identical conditions and evaluated using a multi-objective benchmarking strategy that combines prediction accuracy (RMSE, MAE), variance-explanation capability (R²), and deployment-oriented efficiency metrics (prediction speed, training time, and model size). Across all tensile properties, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) consistently achieved the highest predictive accuracy and variance-explanation capability among the evaluated regression models, with Squared Exponential and Matern 5/2 kernels yielding R² values exceeding 0.98 for Young’s modulus and UTS, and 0.96 for yield strength. The results further suggest that probabilistic kernel-based learning is well suited for modeling the smooth but highly nonlinear structure–property relationships represented in the investigated FeNiCrCoCu molecular dynamics dataset, highlighting the potential of uncertainty-aware regression for interpretable and reliable materials informatics. While compact neural networks and polynomial SVMs provide competitive accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, GPR demonstrated the most balanced performance among the evaluated models in terms of predictive accuracy, robustness, and computational practicality. To ensure transparency, Shapley value–based explainable machine learning is employed to quantify feature contributions and directional effects. The analysis reveals a consistent feature hierarchy across all properties, identifying Cu and Cr contents as the dominant factors associated with the observed tensile-response trends, while grain size and temperature exhibit secondary influence within the investigated MD parameter space. By combining systematic multi-model benchmarking, deployment-aware evaluation, and explainable learning, the proposed X-HEA-ML framework extends conventional black-box prediction by providing interpretable insights that may support tensile-property prediction, alloy screening, and future data-driven HEA design.

science.title: Water-flooded zone identification for ordos Yan9 reservoir using conventional logs
science.description: Accurate identification and evaluation of water-flooded zones play a pivotal role in the efficient exploitation of oil reservoirs, as they directly govern reservoir development adjustment strategies and remaining oil recovery efficiency. In this study, comprehensive analyses of reservoir physical properties, rock electrical parameters, and relative permeability characteristics were conducted by integrating logging data, formation testing data, production performance data, and core test results, based on which a systematic identification method and quantitative evaluation criteria for water-flooded zones were established. The research findings demonstrate that the study area is characterized by an average porosity of 13.8% and an average permeability of 54.7 mD, classifying it as a medium-porosity and medium-permeability reservoir. For the Yan-9 oil formation, the lithology coefficient, saturation exponent, and cementation exponent are determined to be 1.0517, 1.944, and 1.5069, respectively. Three qualitative identification approaches for water-flooded zones-namely, the resistivity comparison method between new and old wells, the porosity-resistivity curve overlay method, and the spontaneous potential baseline shift method—exhibit excellent applicability and reliability in the study area. Furthermore, quantitative classification criteria for water-flooded zones are proposed: low water-flooded zones with Rt > 35 Ω·m and Sw < 35%; medium water-flooded zones with 20 < Rt < 35 Ω·m and 35% < Sw < 50%; and high water-flooded zones with Rt < 20 Ω·m and Sw > 50%. This research not only provides a robust scientific basis for reservoir development adjustment, remaining oil potential assessment, and efficient water control in the study area but also offers valuable insights and references for the identification of water-flooded zones in analogous oil reservoirs worldwide.
